From the client, can we do this and if so, please provide a time estimate: 
 Deleted Contracts

Currently, when a contract is deleted in Alert, it shows as $0 in your report—even though the original total is still on the ticket.

Would it be possible to:
Capture the original Alert total even after deletion and uploaded that total to woo commerce?
Show deleted contracts in the report as a separate total/ category for tracking?

There is no such thing as a deleted contract. Alert has two records (database tables) they are WebRequest and Ticket. A Ticket goes through several phases, Bid, Reservation, Contract, Invoice. We need to be VERY specific about what we're talking about. You can tell from her screenshot, the Ticket has never made it to Contract Phase. It's impossible for this to be a deleted "contract". I realize in "english" a "contract" is any piece of paper with a signature, but in Alert, a Contract. has a VERY specific meaning. We have to be using exact Alert specific language in the requirements.
I can send the screenshot to Alert, but it won't be enough to pinpoint what we need to understand. What I and Alert will really need, is for Layla to fully reproduce the scenario (between 1-3 times) and send us multiple things for each scenario. 1. the woocommerce order number and it's total. 2. the webrequest number. 3. the Ticket number, the phase it was what it deleted, and why its total is different from the woocommerce order /webrequest.

name: Trade Show Experience - Proposal
description:
Latest Feedback from Dina - received 4/30:
I’m so sorry, but I was wrong, and it seems that we do not want to have a drop down list of our upcoming tradeshows that anyone can access. Instead, we are hoping that we can give a link to promoters that they can share with their exhibitors and/or a code that they can put in that will take them to their direct show. The flow would look like:
Tradeshows tab:
For Promoters > Has not changed from the description you have listed.
For Vendors/Exhibitors > Either a popup box to enter in a code for your show or click on this to go to a general tradeshow landing page that asks for a code. (This landing page could be like the promoter section, in having access to the gallery and available tradeshow services, or could just be a basic “Please enter your code here”.)
Once the Exhibitor enters the correct code, they would go into the page for that show, which would be the same as previously discussed.
Pete also mentioned that the dashboard with reporting is not really necessary, unless it is little to no cost.

PROJECT TIME ESTIMATES
Time estimates spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L8k8Z1fcus7K1ucMFJac1UYyp2eI7Ds-Ws_SDa1fUnM/edit?gid=0#gid=0

ORIGINAL DRAW.IO FLOW
https://app.diagrams.net/#G1gBPdNu3g5QqxH_12buMEYf-3KQ4DBkk0#%7B%22pageId%22%3A%227TC7mXn6luR8YCdDC_FC%22%7D


OUTLINE OF PROJECT FOR PROPOSAL PURPOSES
EventRent Trade Show Functionality Summary
The Trade Show section will operate as a separate experience from the standard rental catalog. Users who enter the Trade Show area will follow trade show-specific flows rather than the general rental catalog path.
This section of the website will service two external users:

The Promoter user is the person or organization registering/requesting a trade show to be set up with EventRent. Their flow should stay simple: they submit trade show details through a request form, receive a confirmation email, and EventRent follows up directly.
The Exhibitor/Vendor is the participant in a specific trade show who needs to rent items or request services like freight, labor, power, or internet. They should be able to find their trade show, submit their rental/service request, and optionally use an account if they want to save drafts or reference past submissions.
This experience will be designed and developed for desktop users because of the length of forms and complexity of information expected to be collected and presented.
1. Promoter Flow
Promoters will be able to visit the Trade Show Home page and select an option such as Register a New Trade Show or Request a Trade Show Quote. They will complete a trade show request form with the necessary event details. Once submitted, EventRent will receive the request via email, and the promoter will receive a confirmation email.
The promoter landing page may also include supporting content such as examples of past trade shows, available trade show services, and a gallery of completed trade show setups.
Promoter flows not included
The client specifically requested that we do not build the more complex promoter account functionality, including:
Promoter registration/login requirement
Manual promoter approval process
Promoter “My Account” dashboard
Ability for promoters to view past trade show requests
Ability for promoters to view active trade shows in their account
Ability for promoters to view exhibitor/vendor activity
Promoter-level trade show management tools
The client clarified that most promoters only run one show per year and generally expect EventRent to handle the details after the initial request.
2. Exhibitor / Vendor Flow
Exhibitors will be able to browse a Trade Show List, select their specific trade show, and choose to participate.
The exhibitor experience should allow two paths:
Continue as guest
 Exhibitors can submit their trade show request without creating an account.
Use account accessible via magic link after registration
 Exhibitors may optionally verify their email and access a low-friction account experience using a magic link. This allows them to save/resume drafts and potentially reference previous submissions.
The exhibitor form will include selectable sections such as:
Items
Freight
Labor
Power
Internet, if applicable
These sections should be configurable by trade show, so EventRent can turn certain categories on or off depending on what is offered for that show.
Once submitted, the request will create a Web Request in Alert, send a confirmation email to the exhibitor, and send a separate submission notification to EventRent. Trade show submissions may route to a different internal email than standard website rental requests.
Exhibitor flows not included or reduced
The client requested that we do not require account creation for exhibitors.
The following should not be treated as required functionality:
Mandatory exhibitor registration
Mandatory login before viewing trade shows
Required “My Account” use
Complex historical exhibitor dashboard
Future change request workflow
Full vendor participant management portal
Draft/resume functionality should only be available when an exhibitor chooses to register/verify/login. Guest users will not have draft-saving capability.
3. Trade Show Product and Form Experience
The current paper/PDF form will serve as the foundation for the digital experience, but it does not need to be recreated exactly as one long form.
The item rental sections can be presented similarly to grouped products, allowing exhibitors to browse categories, view pricing, and enter quantities. Categories such as tables, seating, power, internet, freight, and labor may be broken into separate sections or steps.
Freight, storage, and handling may require more custom form logic. The digital form should allow users to enter details such as:
Type of parcel or freight
Quantity
Weight range or weight-based pricing
Dimensions
Description of items
Pre-show and post-show handling needs
Labor calculations may follow the existing paper form structure, with inputs placed into the digital version and calculations handled automatically.
4. Pricing
Each trade show may need to display both early pricing and floor pricing.
The client confirmed there is no simple percentage-based formula for calculating floor pricing from early pricing. Pricing may need to be managed as two separate values.
The site should display the pricing clearly to exhibitors. However, final price handling in Alert Rental may still require EventRent to manually override prices after the WebRequest is submitted.
The WebRequest should include line notes where possible showing the price displayed to the customer and the date/time context of the submission.
5. Payment and Credit Card Authorization
The website will not collect payment as part of this flow.
The trade show checkout/request experience should clearly state that the submission is a request/estimate and that EventRent will follow up. Credit card authorization is not expected to be built directly into this website flow at this stage.
6. Admin / EventRent Back-End Flow
EventRent will need the ability to manage trade show information from the website back end.
Expected admin functionality includes:
Add/edit trade shows
Configure which sections are available per trade show
Manage trade show details and content
Manage pricing information
View submitted trade show requests
Potentially view dashboard-style totals for reporting
The client noted that Dina and Kirsten will likely be the primary users managing the trade show content. Pete may want high-level reporting, so a lightweight dashboard or totals view may be useful.
Potential dashboard metrics may include:
Number of trade show requests per year
Number of exhibitor submissions per year
Active trade shows
Trade show activity over a specific time period
7. Admin flows not required
The client did not express a need for a complex operational dashboard.
The following should be minimized or excluded unless later confirmed:
Promoter registration lists
Vendor registration lists as a primary dashboard feature
Complex pinned trade show dashboards
Full promoter management system
Full exhibitor management system beyond viewing submissions
Advanced reporting unless specifically scoped
Scope Direction
The final scope should focus on a streamlined Trade Show section that allows:
Promoters to submit new trade show requests, exhibitors to select a trade show and submit rental/service requests, EventRent to receive those requests through Alert WebRequest, and EventRent admins to manage trade show content, available sections, pricing, and basic reporting.

Roger the direction and thank you for confirming.

Regarding reporting, what we briefly discussed during our call was a dashboard with summary data. That will enable you, Pete, and any other stakeholders as needed to quickly see the business generated from this investment. Let me/us know if you would like to continue with or without this dashboard.

To stay disciplined with the time this project takes, the better information you feed us, the more efficient we can be. Start with the questions for the "Promoter Registration" and "Trade Show Request" forms you'd like users to fill out. As you map these forms, please think of the following scenarios for the questions:
What are the questions/fields you'd like answered?
If any will have a multiple choice answer, what will those options be for each question
What type of answer field do you want: 
F Name, L Name, email and phone number, and address are stardard fields, any other question you may want to add can be formatted as follows:
short text
long text
yes/no
radio button (allows only one answer to be selected from multiple options)
checkbox (allows multiple answers to be selected from multiple options)

This allows forms to show or hide follow up questions depending on the answer provided. For example, if you ask a promoter "Have you ever worked with us before? > Yes/No," the answer "No" can trigger additional questions to open so you can gather necessary details.
